title: 🧩 Relative Clauses

sections.heading: What they are
sections.body:
Relative clauses add information about a noun using a relative pronoun.

WHO → people (subject): "The student who studies hard..."
WHOM → people (object, formal): "The teacher whom I respect..."
WHICH → things (non-defining): "The report, which was published last year..."
THAT → people or things (defining only): "The study that examined..."
WHOSE → possession: "Students whose results improved..."
WHERE → places: "The university where I studied..."
WHEN → times: "The era when technology advanced..."

sections.heading: Defining vs Non-defining
sections.body:
DEFINING (no commas): identifies WHICH one
"Students who study daily improve faster." → tells us which students

NON-DEFINING (with commas): adds extra information
"My tutor, who has 20 years experience, teaches grammar." → adds info, not identifying

highlight: Non-defining clauses CANNOT use "that". Only "which/who/whose/where". This is a very common Band 6 error.

example.wrong: The book, that I recommended, is excellent.
example.right: The book, which I recommended, is excellent. / The book that I recommended is excellent.

question: Choose the correct relative pronoun: "The researcher _____ discovered this was awarded a prize."
explanation:
"Who" is correct because the researcher is the SUBJECT of the relative clause (they discovered).

"Whom" would be used if they were the object: "The researcher whom I admire..."
"Which" is for things, not people.
"Whose" shows possession.
hint: Is the researcher doing the action or receiving it?

question: Which sentence uses a NON-DEFINING relative clause correctly?
options: Technology which is ubiquitous has changed society.
Technology, which is ubiquitous, has changed society.
Technology, that is ubiquitous, has changed society.
Technology which, is ubiquitous, has changed society.
correct: Technology, which is ubiquitous, has changed society.
explanation:
Non-defining clauses:
✅ Use commas before and after
✅ Use "which" for things (not "that")
✅ Could be removed without changing the core meaning

"Technology, which is ubiquitous, has changed society" = "Technology has changed society" still makes sense.
hint: Non-defining clauses need commas AND cannot use "that".

sentence: The city _______ I grew up has changed enormously since the 1990s.
explanation:
"Where" refers to a place and functions as a locative adverb in the clause.

You could also say "in which" but "where" is more natural and concise — preferred in Band 8+ writing.

❌ "that I grew up" sounds incomplete — needs "in that" which is ungrammatical.
hint: We grew UP somewhere — what relative pronoun introduces a place?

instruction: Match each relative clause to what it describes:
explanation: Mastering pronoun choice is a Band 8 signal. The most commonly confused are who/whom and which/that in defining vs non-defining contexts.

title: Find the Relative Clause Error
instruction: One sentence contains a relative clause error:

sentences.text: The scientists whose research was published received an award.
The city, that was founded in the 12th century, is now a major hub.
sentences.explanation:
"That" cannot be used in NON-DEFINING relative clauses (clauses set off by commas).

✅ Correct: "The city, which was founded in the 12th century, is now a major hub."

sentences.text: Students who fail to plan often struggle with timed essays.
